title: Anthropic closes IPO at $83 a share; IPO plus private placement total about $119.5 billion
summary: Anthropic's public listing is now complete: Class A shares are trading on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT. The announcement sets out the offering price, share counts, and proceeds, and reveals that AMD, NVIDIA, and other chip and cloud giants took part in the concurrent private placement. For regular Claude users, this is capital-markets news — it doesn't change the product or how you use it.
ai_summary: Anthropic announced on Nov. 20 that it had completed its IPO and a concurrent private placement. The deal involved 1.127 billion Class A common shares at $83 each: the company sold about 1.103 billion shares for about $91.6 billion in gross proceeds, while selling stockholders sold about 23.649 million shares, which don't go to the company. Class A shares began trading on Nasdaq under ANT on Nov. 19. The private placement sold about 313 million Class N shares to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and TSMC for about $26.0 billion. Combined gross proceeds from the IPO and private placement came to about $119.5 billion, before underwriting fees. This mainly affects the capital side; the announcement doesn't disclose the post-IPO market cap, use of proceeds, or product plans, and day-to-day use of Claude is unaffected.
brief: Class A shares priced at $83 each, with 1.127 billion shares offered and about 1.103 billion sold by the company.
Underwriters fully exercised the option to purchase an additional 147 million shares.
The concurrent private placement sold about 313 million Class N shares for about $26.0 billion.
The IPO and private placement together raised about $119.5 billion in gross proceeds, before underwriting fees and other expenses.

sections.h: What happened: Anthropic closes its IPO

blocks.p: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, announced on Nov. 20 that it had closed its initial public offering and a concurrent private placement. Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov. 19 under the symbol ANT.

This is a closing notice. The substance is how many shares were issued, at what price, who bought them, and how much the company received. It says nothing about products, models, or subscription pricing. For scale: our earlier coverage shows Anthropic raised $65 billion in Series H funding before the IPO at a $965 billion post-money valuation — note that's the previous round's valuation, not this IPO's market cap.

sections.h: How many shares the IPO sold and what Anthropic received

blocks.p: The IPO offered 1,127,000,000 Class A common shares at $83.00 per share. Of those, Anthropic sold 1,103,351,354 shares, or about 1.103 billion, and selling stockholders sold 23,648,646 shares, or about 23.649 million.

The underwriters also fully exercised the overallotment option — the greenshoe, an extra block of shares reserved at the time of the offering. They bought an additional 147 million shares at the original offering price. A fully used greenshoe typically signals strong demand.

On a gross basis, before underwriting discounts, commissions, and other offering expenses, the IPO raised about $93.5 billion, of which about $91.6 billion went to Anthropic. Proceeds from shares sold by selling stockholders don't go to the company.

sections.h: Concurrent private placement: tech giants buy $26 billion of Class N stock

blocks.p: Alongside the public offering, Anthropic completed a private placement: it sold 313,253,007 shares of Class N common stock to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and TSMC at the same $83.00 per-share price, for about $26.0 billion in total.

The buyers are concentrated in chips, cloud computing, and foundry. The announcement says only that these Class N shares weren't registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and were sold as a private placement. It doesn't explain how Class N shares differ from Class A in voting rights, conversion, or dividends.
Add the IPO — including shares sold by selling stockholders — and the private placement, and total gross proceeds come to about $119.5 billion, again before underwriting fees and other expenses.

blocks.p: According to the announcement, the SEC declared the registration statement effective on Nov. 18, Class A shares began trading on Nov. 19, and the closing was announced on Nov. 20. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were the lead book-running managers, with J.P. Morgan, Citigroup, Barclays, Wells Fargo Securities, and several other banks acting as underwriters.

list: Post-IPO market cap: the announcement gives no total shares outstanding, no market cap, and no valuation implied by the IPO.
Net proceeds after fees: it discloses only gross proceeds, not the net amount after underwriting discounts and commissions.
How Class N shares differ from Class A: voting rights, convertibility, and dividends aren't specified.
Use of proceeds: it doesn't say how the roughly $119.5 billion in gross proceeds will be spent.
Who the selling stockholders were and how much they received: the document refers only to "certain selling stockholders."
Impact on Claude products, pricing, or compute: the announcement doesn't mention it.

blocks.p: Value: this release makes the scale of Anthropic's IPO and private placement clear. It's for readers who want to verify hard facts like the offering price, share counts, and participants, and it's a useful size reference for anyone following capital flows in the AI industry.
Cost: it's only a closing notice, with no product, technology, or business updates — and all amounts are gross proceeds before fees.

If you're following ANT, focus on the prospectus and future earnings reports rather than this announcement alone. If you're a Claude user, nothing about your experience changes and there's no action to take. If you just want the scale: $83 per share, and about $119.5 billion in combined IPO and private-placement gross proceeds.
